channel.title: SSbusinessAndMarket
channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from SSbusinessAndMarket, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: Despite China's 996 culture, DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng says his workers don't do overtime or even have KPIs: 'No one manages them'
item.description: While Silicon Valley adopts China's 996 culture, DeepSeek's founder says his $60 billion AI company has no KPIs and no overtime.

item.title: Christopher Nolan's Odyssey communicates a timeless — and tragic — aspect of war
item.description: Matt Damon's Odysseus dramatizes a condition clinicians call moral injury — distinct from PTSD — that still affects veterans today.

item.title: Wall Street's hidden recruiting pipeline isn't an Ivy League diploma—it's the teammate who triples your odds of getting hired
item.description: A study of over 120,000 Ivy League graduates finds that locker room ties, not diplomas, are the real gatekeepers into top finance firms.

item.title: Andy Jassy envisions a $1 trillion cloud business, citing clients like the PGA Tour that replaced server trucks with AI broadcasts
item.description: AWS reported $42.2 billion in revenue with its fastest growth in 18 quarters, and AI platform spending last quarter exceeded all prior quarters combined.
